thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Dedicated pool 'saffron-dedpool' node saffron-node-12 reported repeated NVLINK lane errors. Severity: potential multi-GPU job disruption. Automatic routing to fallback pool triggered.

marie: I have the page, taking lead. tagging @devon for hardware ops, @tess for runtime mitigation, @sophie for CS/customer comms.

devon: on it. first glance, nvlink lane 2 errors + ECC counters rising on GPU1/GPU2. pulling recent dmesg and nvlink logs.

devon: logs show repeated link flaps, sample: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia: nvlink: link 2 status change -> lane parity error
[ 1234.568200] nvidia: nvlink: lane 2 reset attempt 1
[ 1234.569000] nvidia: gpu1: mc: ecc corrected errors++
```

tess: thanks. can we drain multi-GPU pods off saffron-node-12? prefer graceful move to keep in-flight requests consistent.

devon: starting drain now. command: `redwood node drain --pool saffron-dedpool --node saffron-node-12 --mode graceful --timeout 600s`

oliver: FYI I'm watching routing. We already routed new multi-GPU allocations away; some low-latency single-GPU inferences are still using the node. Will force migrate those next if they hit errors.

sophie: contacting Saffron Labs AM/engineer on call, sending initial impact note: "We observed NVLINK errors on one dedicated node in your pool. We're draining the node and migrating workloads to maintain SLAs. We'll provide updates as we know more."

marie: Incident priority: P2 (customer-facing but fallback mitigations available). Logging incident in ops tracker (INC-2026).

devon: drain progress: 6/8 multi-gpu pods re-scheduled, 2 pods still terminating (long-running batch). ETA 4m.

incident-bot: Deploybot: deploy to saffron-dedpool is paused due to node drain.

tess: while we drain, I'm enabling a routing policy to prefer model-compat single-GPU variants for Saffron tenant to avoid multi-GPU fallback failures. patch in routing-service: 
```json
{"tenant":"saffron","policy":"prefer_single_gpu_variant","ttl":300}
```

marie: good. @devon after drain completes can you mark node as `maintenance` and open a hardware ticket with vendor (NVLINK diagnostics)? include NVLINK logs & ECC counters.

devon: opened HW ticket HW-5543 with vendor, attaching logs and kernel traces. vendor assigned contact: kai.

kai: acknowledged. we'll schedule an on-site or remote diag depending on early triage. initial suspicion: degraded NVLINK retimer or cable.

oliver: monitoring metrics: Saffron 99th latency spiked 30% during fail window for multi-GPU pipelines; overall error rate increased 0.8%. Most traffic now on fallback pool, so customer impact should be limited.

sophie: Saffron replied: "Thanks for the quick action. We're seeing a handful of failing requests but overall degraded throughput. Please share ETA for node replacement and any configuration changes we should expect."

marie: reply to Saffron: "We're draining the affected node and migrating workloads. Expect full replacement in 6–12 hours pending vendor confirmation. We've enabled single-GPU routing for your tenant to stabilize latency. Will update within 30m or sooner."

devon: drain finished. node saffron-node-12 state=drained. moving to maintenance. command: `redwood node set-state saffron-node-12 maintenance`

devon: also snapshotting GPU firmware & nvlink state for vendor: `redwood hw export --node saffron-node-12 --artifacts nvlink,fw,ecclogs --out /tmp/saffron-node-12-artifacts.tar.gz`

tess: runtime mitigation checklist complete: 
- drained node
- routing policy updated
- fallback pool capacity verified (10% headroom)
- cache warmers primed on fallback

oliver: rolling alert for similar NVLINK patterns across other saffron nodes for next 2 hours. I'll escalate if correlated. so far isolated.

kai: vendor triage suggests remote retimer firmware attempt first. if that fails, replace NIC riser / cabling. ETA for remote attempt: 90m.

sophie: told customer we'll try remote fix first. noted they'll want a follow-up postmortem for SLA impact. setting calendar invite for a 1h check-in.

marie: handoff plan: I'm on for initial containment. I'll hand to @devon for follow-ups after 30m. creating a follow-up thread in #postmortems with the incident id.

devon: taking follow-up. next steps: monitor fallback pool, coordinate vendor remote diag, schedule replacement if remote fix fails, update customer at each milestone.

sophie: customer acknowledges and appreciates the quick mitigation. requests a short status email once vendor confirms.

tess: dropping a quick runbook note for ops: 
```
If NVLINK lane errors observed on dedicated node:
1) Immediate: `redwood node drain --node <node> --mode graceful`
2) Update routing: prefer single-gpu variants for tenant
3) Verify fallback pool headroom
4) Open vendor HW ticket with NVLINK logs
5) Snapshot firmware & ecc logs
6) Mark node maintenance and schedule diag/replace
```

marie: great. setting incident state -> monitoring. tagging Postmortem owner: @devon. will update incident tracker with timeline. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 status updated -> monitoring.

devon: vendor remote retimer attempt completed — no improvement. vendor recommends hardware replacement. prepping procurement and ETA 6–12h for field swap.

sophie: sent customer update with replacement ETA and temporary mitigations. they asked for traffic logs; attached 10m window.

marie: closing active mitigation loop; leaving on-call watch for 2 hours then hand to next oncall. follow-up items for postmortem: root cause, replacement timeline, routing policy test coverage.

devon: leaving notes in the node ticket: replace riser/cable + run nvlink acceptance tests after swap.

kai: field replacement scheduled. will provide swap completion ts once done.

marie: thanks all. moving to status=watching. we'll reconvene after swap or if new alerts fire. :eyes:
